audit_after: the cost-of-capital lever. THIS REBUILD IS MOSTLY RECORD-SHAPE AND THAT IS THE REASON THE AUDIT POINT SITS WHERE IT DOES. Of the exemplar's outstanding entries, nine close by committing a record the sanctioned modules already emit — the driver lines, the asset base, the anchor ordering, the rebuild ledger itself — and NONE OF THOSE CAN MOVE THE CENTRAL, because under [R-LENS-03] the class primary IS the central and a record commit does not touch the cash-flow lens. The circularity-block unit correction feeds a CROSS-CHECK, which by the same rule is published beside the answer and never averaged into it. So exactly one lever has a route to the number: rebuilding the cost of capital through cost_of_capital.py, which moves the discount rate and therefore the DCF. The place to stop and look is after that lever and BEFORE the document is rebuilt — because once a figure is written into a delivered document the next reader takes it as settled, and because the terminal is STOPPED (TERMINAL_EVIDENCE_05-09-2026.md, three independent disclosure gaps), so the single largest construction in this study is NOT among the levers and cannot offset whatever the discount rate does.

levers.name: relative-lens circularity block put on one basis
levers.why: The non-circularity block compared an AED spot with a share count in millions against an equity value in USD thousands, so the traded multiple it published was 0.9909x — a number in no units at all. Put on one basis it is 6.92x. This feeds a CROSS-CHECK, which under [R-LENS-03] is published beside the central and never averaged into it, so the central does not move.
levers.evidence: lens_record.cross_checks[1].circularity now carries spot 1.6773 USD, shares 7,398,499 thousand and a basis field naming the units

levers.name: the bridge declares its currency, scale and peg
levers.why: The bridge divides USD thousands by a share count the field name calls millions, and converts to dirhams at the peg only at the per-share step. The generator said so IN A COMMENT and a gate reading the record reported the exemplar as carrying the largest bridge disagreement in the book — 1.5263 against a published 5.6054, which are the same number either side of the 3.6725 peg. A comment in a builder is not a declaration a reader or a checker can use.
levers.evidence: bridge_record.units: currency USD, scale thousands, per_share USD, published AED, fx 3.6725

levers.name: the third tranche of the capital structure is declared
levers.why: Equity 0.800444 and drawn debt 0.071933 sum to 0.872377, and the remaining 0.127635 is the perpetual capital securities — real, priced at their own disclosed coupon and in this model since the first edition, but committed in a different object. The three weights sum to one EXACTLY and reproduce the published WACC to zero, so no rate and no value moves; what was missing was the declaration. The gate was re-pointed rather than the number changed [R-COC-01].
levers.evidence: cost_of_capital_record.other_tranches + beta_source; check_ke_reproduction now reproduces ADNOCLS and it is off that ratchet

levers.name: the fleet is committed with the date it was true on
levers.why: On a chartered fleet valued with replacement cost beside the cash-flow lens the fleet IS the asset base. The study already held it at three sourced vintages — 53 owned tankers at 31 December 2025, one very large crude carrier sold in January 2026, eleven vessels bought on 7 August 2026 — and stated the vintage of none of them where anything outside the study could read it. 156 owned vessels as at 7 August 2026, components footing to the total, against an information set ending 1Q2026.
levers.evidence: asset_base_record + information_set_ends; off the asset-base ratchet

levers.name: the profit anchor ordering, measured rather than asserted
levers.why: The bridge stands on the reviewed 31 March 2026 sheet and the margin is anchored on the AUDITED FY2025 year, 90 days behind it, and the record did not say why — leaving a reader to assume the study opened that filing and took half of it. It did not: every line of the Q1 2026 income statement is registered and consumed. A margin is a rate over a full cycle of this company's own contract book and one reviewed quarter is a point on a seasonal path.
levers.evidence: 1Q2026 computes 32.73% on the same construction against the 29.28% anchored — the LOWER of the two is adopted, so the forecast faces the stricter comparison and the choice cannot be flattering it

levers.name: the driver lines and the cost basis behind them
levers.why: The study built seven driver lines, ran the ground-up assertion on them and committed only what the assertion RETURNED. Running it from outside found a real gap on the exemplar: four of the seven named how revenue was built and nothing about how cost was — the margin-is-the-input treatment written into each gap note and not into the field a checker reads.
levers.evidence: driver_lines committed; 2 ground-up assertions now actually run across the book where 1 did

levers.name: the reporting scale, so the earnings reconciliation can be read
levers.why: shares_mn carries its scale in its name and npa_fy25 carries none, so an instrument dividing one into the other lands a factor of a thousand out — which the gate reported, correctly, as a reconciliation it could not read rather than a defect it could see. A magnitude test would have "resolved" a real error as cleanly as a scale.
levers.evidence: reporting_units{USD, thousands, millions, AED, 3.6725}; EPS now reconciles at 0.1133 computed against 0.1100 reported

levers.name: the delivered pages: retired blend, retired verdict, edition date, both prices
levers.why: The numbers file had retired the blend for weeks and the DOCUMENTS had not: five assertions of a weighted central, three of a skill score against a random-walk benchmark that [R-CAL-03] retired outright, a caption claiming contributions that add to a central they no longer build, no edition date in the masthead at all, and one price on a page where the rule asks for two.
levers.evidence: off the lens-vocabulary, band and edition ratchets; the study's own four stale label expectations re-pointed; 813 prose figures, 63 tables, 169 labels, 111 drivers and 119 recalculations all green

note: Declared 07-09-2026 BEFORE any lever was applied, per [R-REBUILD-01]. The start spot is the LATEST KNOWN price of 6.80 (07-09-2026, supplied by the principal and committed to engine/prices/SUPPLIED_07-09-2026.json) rather than the 6.16 this study was struck at: the committed central of 5.6054 sat 9.0% below the struck price and sits 17.6% below the latest, so this study acquired a gap breach WITHOUT ANY LEVER MOVING, which is [R-GAP-01 AMENDED]'s own finding and is recorded here as the starting condition rather than discovered at the end.

stopped.lever: the terminal on a disclosed asset life
stopped.why: STOPPED, not deferred. TERMINAL_EVIDENCE_05-09-2026.md records three independent reasons the accounts yield no usable life: dry-docking is capitalised and amortised over two to five years while the vessel line is not split by component; one vessel class prints its age as an unfilled placeholder; and 97.85% of depreciable net book value sits in a single column spanning six disclosed lives from 2 to 40 years. A LIFE THIS DESK CHOSE IS NOT A DISCLOSED LIFE (SIGCM clause 1), so this rebuild does not touch the terminal and the ratchet entry stands.

audit.reached: the declared audit point — after the cost-of-capital lever and before the document is rebuilt.
audit.finding: EVERY LEVER SO FAR HAS MOVED THE RECORD AND NONE HAS MOVED THE ANSWER. The central is 5.605379 after four levers exactly as it was before the first, and that is the honest result rather than a disappointing one: four standing rules were breached by this study, all four are now met, and not one of them was a wrong number. The cost-of-capital lever was expected to be the only one with a route to the central and it turned out to have none either — the weights were already right and only undeclared.
audit.consequence: The gap is therefore unchanged by the rebuild and is entirely the price moving: 5.6054 against 6.80 is -17.6%, past [R-GAP-01]'s ten per cent trigger, so this study owes its eight-heading review before any file is staged, and [R-GAP-02] holds it from publishing either way. THE REVIEW IS NOT A FORMALITY HERE: the largest single construction in this study, the terminal, is STOPPED for want of a disclosed asset life, so the one place a defect of this size would most likely sit is the one place this rebuild could not look.
audit.after_the_audit_point: FOUR FURTHER LEVERS, and the audit point held: the finding it recorded — that every lever moves the record and none moves the answer — survived all four. Recorded here rather than folded into the levers above, because a route walked after the stop is still a route somebody chose to keep walking.
